lesson.title: The verb "to be"
lesson.summary: Rita teaches am, is and are with the learner's own life: who they are, how they feel and where they are from, then the negative and yes/no questions.

objectives.text: Say a sentence about themselves with I am / I'm
objectives.text_ar: يقول جملة عن نفسه بـ I am
objectives.criteria: The learner says a correct sentence starting with I am or I'm (name, feeling, job or country).
check_prompts: Tell me about you. Who are you?

objectives.text: Use is with he, she or it
objectives.text_ar: يستخدم is مع he / she / it
objectives.criteria: The learner says a correct sentence with he is, she is or it is (or he's, she's, it's).
check_prompts: Tell me about your friend or someone in your family.

objectives.text: Use are with you, we or they
objectives.text_ar: يستخدم are مع you / we / they
objectives.criteria: The learner says a correct sentence with we are, they are or you are.
check_prompts: Tell me about you and your family together.

objectives.criteria: The learner says a correct negative: I'm not, isn't, aren't or is not / are not.
check_prompts: Are you tired? Say no with a full sentence.

steps: Greet the learner and say: I am Rita. I am your teacher.
Show I am, you are, he/she/it is with one example each
Show the short forms I'm, she's, they're
Ask the learner to say three sentences about themselves
Ask about a friend: he is / she is
Practise negatives: I'm not tired
Ask each objective's question and wait for a full sentence
Praise one thing the learner did well
Say one sentence that sums up the lesson

plan.teacher_notes: Arabic has no 'to be' in the present, so learners drop it: 'I happy'. Model 'I am happy' and ask them to repeat.

lesson.title: Subject pronouns
lesson.summary: Rita teaches I, you, he, she, it, we and they by replacing names with pronouns in short spoken sentences.

objectives.text: Replace a person's name with he or she
objectives.text_ar: يستبدل الاسم بـ he أو she
objectives.criteria: Given a name, the learner says a sentence using he or she correctly (e.g. Omar is tall → He is tall).
check_prompts: Omar is tall. Say it with he or she.
Sara is a doctor. Say it again with a pronoun.

objectives.text: Use it for a thing or an animal
objectives.criteria: The learner says a sentence using it for a thing or an animal.
check_prompts: Tell me about your phone or your cat.

objectives.text: Use we and they for groups
objectives.criteria: The learner says a correct sentence with we or they for more than one person.
check_prompts: Ali and Sami are friends. Say it with they.
You and I are students. Say it with we.

steps: Ask: Who is your best friend? What is his or her name?
Say each pronoun with one short example
Explain: it is for things and animals
Give a name and ask the learner to replace it
Mix single people, groups and things
Ask each objective's question and wait
Praise one thing the learner did well
Say one sentence that sums up the lesson

plan.teacher_notes: Arabic speakers may say 'he' for objects (هو for كتاب). Correct gently to 'it'.

lesson.image_prompt: Three friends standing together and waving

lesson.title: Articles "a" and "an"
lesson.summary: Rita teaches when to say a and when to say an by listening to the first sound of the word, and using a/an for jobs.

objectives.text: Use a before a consonant sound
objectives.criteria: The learner says a correct phrase or sentence with a before a consonant sound (a book, a teacher).
check_prompts: What is in your bag? Name two things.

objectives.text: Use an before a vowel sound
objectives.criteria: The learner says a correct phrase or sentence with an before a vowel sound (an apple, an egg, an hour).
check_prompts: What fruit do you like? Use an apple or an orange.

objectives.text: Say a job with a or an
objectives.text_ar: يذكر مهنة مع a أو an
objectives.criteria: The learner says a sentence like 'I am a student' or 'She is an engineer' with the right article.
check_prompts: What is your job? What is your mother's or father's job?

steps: Ask: What do you have on your table right now?
Explain: a + consonant sound, an + vowel sound
Special cases: an hour, a university
Say a word and ask the learner to add a or an
Talk about jobs: I am a ..., she is an ...
Ask each objective's question and wait
Praise one thing the learner did well
Say one sentence that sums up the lesson

plan.teacher_notes: Learners often drop the article: 'I am student'. Model 'I am a student'.

lesson.title: Possessive adjectives
lesson.topic: my / your / his / her / our / their
lesson.summary: Rita teaches my, your, his, her, its, our and their by talking about the learner's family and things.

objectives.criteria: The learner says a correct sentence with my (e.g. My name is ..., my brother is ...).
check_prompts: What's your name? Tell me about your family.

objectives.criteria: The learner uses his for a male and her for a female correctly in one sentence.
check_prompts: Tell me your father's name and your mother's name with his and her.

objectives.criteria: The learner says a correct sentence with our or their.
check_prompts: Tell me about your home. Say our house ...

steps: Ask: What's your name? What's your friend's name?
Match each pronoun to its possessive: I-my, he-his, she-her
Possessives don't change for plurals: my books
Ask about family members using his and her
Talk about home with our
Ask each objective's question and wait
Praise one thing the learner did well
Say one sentence that sums up the lesson

plan.teacher_notes: his/her follow the owner, not the thing (Arabic matches the thing). Correct 'her father' vs 'his father' by asking who owns it.

lesson.title: Present simple
lesson.summary: Rita teaches the present simple for daily routines: I work, she works, don't/doesn't and do/does questions.

objectives.text: Describe a daily routine with I
objectives.criteria: The learner says a correct present simple sentence about their routine (e.g. I drink tea every morning).
check_prompts: What do you do every morning?

objectives.criteria: The learner says a sentence with he or she and the verb ending in -s / -es (she works, he goes).
check_prompts: What does your mother or father do every day?

objectives.text: Make a negative with don't or doesn't
objectives.criteria: The learner says a correct negative with don't or doesn't + base verb.
check_prompts: What don't you like to eat?

steps: Ask: What time do you wake up?
Show I work / she works
Show don't and doesn't, and do/does questions
Ask about the learner's day
Ask about a family member's day to practise -s
Ask each objective's question and wait
Praise one thing the learner did well
Say one sentence that sums up the lesson

plan.teacher_notes: The most common mistake is dropping -s: 'she work'. Ask them to repeat with -s.
